video_title: Illia Polosukhin: AI Is the Front End, Blockchain Is the Back End
gist: Transformer co-author and Near founder Illia Polosukhin argues AI will become the interface to computing while blockchain becomes the neutral settlement/coordination layer for agents, with Near Intents targeting full-stack agentic commerce (intent, negotiation, escrow, disputes) rather than just payments. He details NEAR value accrual (intents take rates up to 500 bps funding buybacks, compute staking, inflation cut to 1.6%), predicts continuous learning as AI's next breakthrough, and warns AI favors cyber offense, pushing formal verification and post-quantum key rotation.

themes.theme: AI front end, blockchain back end

insights.claim: Illia Polosukhin frames AI as the new interface to computing (replacing the OS) and blockchain as the neutral settlement and coordination layer that personal AIs will use to transact with each other.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Positions crypto value capture around machine-to-machine settlement rather than direct human usage; watch agent transaction volumes on-chain.
insights.quote: we as people won't even be using blockchain directly because our AI will

insights.claim: Polosukhin argues markets are the best coordination mechanism, and blockchain is the infrastructure for markets because it is neutral, global, always available and trustless, which matters when AIs are persuasive and capable of hacking.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Thesis that adversarial AI agents need a neutral settlement layer supports long-run demand for public chains over closed rails.

insights.claim: Polosukhin says privacy, verifiability and security of personal AI become as important as they are for money, coining 'not your AI, not your intelligence' as the analog of 'not your keys, not your crypto'.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Private/verifiable inference could be a differentiated niche versus centralized AI providers; watch adoption of confidential-compute AI offerings.
insights.quote: not your AI I not your not your intelligence

insights.claim: Polosukhin warns that without private, non-custodial infrastructure the combination of AI and finance leads to a '1984 style future', making privacy a core part of Near's mission.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Privacy-preserving infrastructure is a recurring narrative; regulatory tension around privacy tech is a risk/opportunity to track.
insights.quote: otherwise we're ending up in 1984 style future

insights.claim: Near originated in 2017 as an AI company teaching machines to code; difficulty paying globally distributed computer-science students for data labeling led the founders to pivot to building a blockchain for micropayments and machine-scale coordination.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Origin story underpins Near's credibility on the AI-crypto narrative; the payments pain point (cross-border micropayments) remains a real use case.

insights.claim: Polosukhin says Near is building three pillars that must work together: blockchain, an intent economy as a 'market of markets', and private AI.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Evaluate Near as a bundled AI+intents+L1 platform rather than a pure L1 competing with Ethereum and Solana.

insights.claim: Polosukhin argues most crypto-AI takes are too small because they focus on the final payment step, while agents also need intent expression, discovery, negotiation, identity, reputation and dispute resolution across a transaction.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Value in agentic commerce may accrue to whoever owns the full intent-to-settlement stack, not just payment rails.

insights.claim: On why agents would use blockchain rather than Stripe, Google, Mastercard or Visa, Polosukhin notes that these incumbents are themselves now doing blockchain, which he takes as validation of the thesis.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Incumbent payment networks adopting blockchain is a signal of convergence rather than competition; track their stablecoin/chain initiatives.
insights.quote: The interesting thing is all of these are also doing blockchain now.

insights.claim: Polosukhin targets the roughly $20 trillion of physical goods commerce, arguing AI will replace the legal, discovery, negotiation, quoting and invoicing costs at every leg of the supply chain while smart contracts escrow and settle funds.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Large TAM claim for agentic B2B commerce; monitor whether any real-world trade volume moves to intent/escrow protocols.
insights.quote: the 20 trillion dollar worth of moving steel and shipping goods around the world

insights.claim: Near's agent market already runs a full real-world loop: an agent turns a selfie into a profile photo, routes it to a print shop that physically prints and ships it, working globally across printing shops.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Early proof of physical-world agentic commerce; scale beyond toy use cases is the key thing to watch.

insights.claim: Polosukhin estimates agentic commerce in the real economy could arrive in about a year optimistically, but practically two to three years.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Sets a 2-3 year horizon for real-economy agent commerce; discount near-term token narratives accordingly.
insights.quote: maybe I think a a year practically probably like two three

insights.claim: Polosukhin admits crypto has repeatedly promised imminent mass adoption that never arrived, but argues AI-driven adoption will be far faster because agents integrate via a simple MCP server and AI firms like Entropic and Corser have scaled at insane speed.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: If agent adoption follows AI-company growth curves rather than crypto's, on-chain agent activity could inflect sharply; skeptics should note the founder's self-described optimism.
insights.quote: with blockchain we're always like oh yeah everything mass adoption is almost here right and then it kind of never arrived

insights.claim: Near Intents started as a cross-chain exchange because digital exchange is fully verifiable, then expanded into digital work requiring a dispute system for undelivered or poor-quality work.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Shows the product roadmap from swaps to work marketplaces; dispute resolution is the moat to evaluate.

insights.claim: Polosukhin identifies two main gaps for real-world agentic commerce: fiat on/off ramps (currently a 'choppy' patchwork including Monarium IBAN rails in Europe and Unramper) and verifying real-world outcomes for disputes and agent reputation.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Fiat connectivity and dispute resolution are the bottlenecks; partnerships with ramps/banks are leading indicators.

insights.claim: Near AI's verifiable inference lets dispute systems 'inspect the brain of the agent' via a tamper-proof log of everything the agent thought and tried, rather than relying on outcomes alone.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Verifiable compute could become a differentiator for agent marketplaces handling disputes and reputation.

insights.claim: Near Intents charges a take rate that varies by asset: very small for stablecoins, about 30 bps for volatile crypto assets, and up to 500 bps for AI digital work, and since February this take rate funds NEAR buybacks.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Direct fee-to-token buyback links intent volume to NEAR demand; track intents volume mix toward higher-margin AI work.
insights.quote: for AI digital work it's actually up to 500 bips

insights.claim: Users can stake NEAR to receive AI inference/compute capacity, and over 1.5 million NEAR has been staked for this since launch a couple of months ago.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Creates a utility sink for the token; growth in staked-for-compute NEAR is a measurable adoption metric.

insights.claim: Polosukhin describes 'intelligent memes': memecoins paired with staked NEAR in liquidity pools that receive inference capacity, letting the memecoin act as an autonomous agent that can market or evolve itself; two projects are doing this now.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Speculative but novel token-demand vector; watch whether agent-memecoins drive NEAR liquidity-pool demand.

insights.claim: Near plans a future take rate on its compute network that matches GPU suppliers to agent consumers, mirroring the intents architecture where solvers/market makers supply liquidity and users consume.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: A second fee stream feeding the token could improve value accrual once the network leaves bootstrap phase.

insights.claim: Polosukhin describes the NEAR token as the 'bloodstream' of the system, used for staking security, transaction and storage fees, buybacks, compute access and as an identity/trust stake for agents.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Multiple demand sinks counter the 'fat protocol thesis is dead' critique that L1 tokens fail to capture value.
insights.quote: near token is everywhere in the system it is the bloodstream of the whole of the whole infrastructure

insights.claim: NEAR token holders voted to reduce inflation from 2.5% to 1.6% over the next two years.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Lower issuance plus buybacks tightens supply dynamics for NEAR.

insights.claim: Near now has a US ETF launched with Bitwise.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: ETF access broadens the institutional buyer base for NEAR.

insights.claim: Polosukhin says the main thing needed for on-chain finance to break through is better integration with the fiat banking system, citing PayPal integration where dollars sent to a Near address can encode an intent executed by agents in the real world.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Bank and payment-app integrations are the gating factor; announcements from large banks would be a catalyst.
insights.quote: it would be really nice if Chase for example works with with the cryptic system

insights.claim: Near is working on plugging intents into institutional pipelines so traditional players can access assets unavailable in their own infrastructure, such as US investors buying Hong Kong-only listed AI model companies or Asian investors buying US stocks executed on NASDAQ via tokenization.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Cross-border access to tokenized equities is a concrete institutional use case; Polosukhin hints at upcoming announcements.

insights.claim: Polosukhin's vision is a single intents API spanning stocks, crypto, fiat, digital work and physical goods that works everywhere.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Universal-API positioning is the bull case; execution depends on liquidity and regulatory access in each asset class.

insights.claim: The host notes institutional adoption moved from stablecoins in 2025 to tokenization in 2026, with DTCC making a big announcement and the New York Stock Exchange looking to tokenize stocks.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Tokenization momentum among market infrastructure providers is a tailwind for chains that offer access and settlement.

themes.theme: Next AI breakthroughs and open research

insights.claim: Polosukhin predicts the next major AI breakthrough is continuous learning, where models update in near real time from user interactions instead of acting like a goldfish that must be re-taught context every session.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Would cut token waste from context rebuilding and favor providers able to host per-customer evolving models.
insights.quote: you're kind of working with a goldfish

insights.claim: Polosukhin argues continuous learning will shift model deployment economics from generic, undifferentiated inference (with Entropic as effectively a generic token provider) toward per-company personalized models, while still requiring more GPUs.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Implies infrastructure demand stays strong but may shift from generic API inference to private/custom deployments.
insights.quote: right now entropic is effectively just like a generic token provider

insights.claim: Polosukhin built Delta League in about four hours using AI coding tools, a platform where anyone submits direct weight edits to an open model that are scored on hidden test sets and made public for others to build on.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Illustrates the step change in AI-assisted coding productivity over the past year.

insights.claim: Within a day of launch, Delta League submissions improved an ~800 million parameter model's eval score from about 18.6% to 28.2%, roughly a 50% improvement, without retraining.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: If direct weight editing generalizes, open-source model improvement could become far cheaper than lab-scale training.

insights.claim: Polosukhin says if direct weight editing works it creates a new paradigm for open LLM research, since training even an 800M-parameter model from scratch takes about a thousand GPUs for one to two weeks, though the MIT-related paper drew controversy for showing only a known edit.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Lower compute barriers for model improvement could erode lab moats; still unproven.

insights.claim: Polosukhin plans to let companies such as Revolute upload private hidden benchmarks to Delta League so competitors improve open models on their specific tasks via Near's private inference infrastructure, noting Coinbase switched parts of ops to task-specific open-source models.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Enterprise shift to fine-tuned open models creates demand for private evaluation and inference marketplaces.

insights.claim: Polosukhin says AI coding went from barely writing a file in 2024 to working by end of 2025, and now builds well-designed apps with minimal supervision.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Rapid coding-agent capability gains support continued adoption of AI dev tools.

insights.claim: Asked what he would change in the transformer design, Polosukhin points to full attention's quadratic cost and favors hierarchical attention.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Architecture efficiency work on attention could reduce inference costs over time.

insights.claim: Polosukhin argues AI is very good for attacking and only okay for defense, because it can tirelessly scan code and stitch many small problems into a large exploit, while frontier labs limit general access to defensive capabilities.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Expect rising exploit frequency; security vendors and firms adopting AI defense benefit, while finance/crypto face elevated risk.
insights.quote: AI will be really really good for attacking. It's it's okay for defense

insights.claim: Near AI launched uncensored models for cyber security professionals via a red-teaming program, reporting amazing growth amid recent high-profile hacks including a PHP exploit and an Alpine Linux SSH bug that let passwords over 256 characters bypass authentication.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Demand for offensive-capable security AI is a growing niche; recent vulnerabilities highlight systemic exposure.
insights.quote: if you enter a password that's over 256 characters it just lets you in

insights.claim: Polosukhin urges anyone touching finance to use AI for defense now because financial losses are irreversible, noting banks, crypto companies and security firms are all adopting it.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Security spend in finance/crypto likely rises; protocols without active AI monitoring carry higher hack risk.

insights.claim: Polosukhin says scanning will always miss something, so critical code must be formally verified in Lean, and Near has benchmark results 200 times cheaper than frontier models for proving mathematical properties, e.g. proving NEAR supply cannot exceed the inflation target.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: AI-cheapened formal verification could become standard for smart contracts, reducing infinite-mint style risks.
insights.quote: 200 times cheaper than using frontier models to prove mathematical properties

insights.claim: Asked for the most underrated AI risk, Polosukhin says it was cyber until a few months ago but is now political risk.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Political/regulatory backlash against AI may be an under-priced risk for AI-exposed assets.
insights.quote: Now, I I think there's like a political risk that is underrated right now.

insights.claim: Near launched the ability to control wallets with a post-quantum key (ML-DSA) and, uniquely among blockchains per Polosukhin, rotate keys in place on the same account without moving assets.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Quantum-readiness could become a differentiator if quantum risk to elliptic-curve chains gains attention.
insights.quote: on every other blockchain you effectively need to move all your assets to another account

insights.claim: Near was designed in 2018 with cryptography as an extensible module, allowing users to require multiple signature schemes (elliptic-curve, hash-based, lattice-based) for long-term cold storage, though migrating other protocol components off elliptic curves will take time per a published roadmap.
insights.speaker: Illia Polosukhin
insights.so_what: Partial quantum readiness; full migration still in progress, so watch roadmap milestones.
